doc.about.title: About Ask Brasil
doc.about.lede: What this service is, and where the answers come from.
doc.about.body:
## What it is
Ask Brasil helps you find and understand Brazilian federal services. Ask a question in your own words, in Portuguese or English, and get a short answer with a link to the exact official page it came from. When a question takes more than words, Ask Brasil adds a tool to the conversation.

## What it is not
Ask Brasil is an independent service. It is not the Federal Government and does not speak for any ministry. It never signs in on your behalf, files a request or takes a payment. For those steps it points you to the official site.

## Where the answers come from
Answers come from official pages on gov.br and other Government of Brazil domains, and from open public data such as IBGE's and the Central Bank's. Every figure and date shows when it was checked.

## Open and adoptable
Ask Brasil follows federal web standards: accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), Brazil's General Data Protection Law and strict security. It is built so that a government team could adopt and run it.
doc.privacy.title: Privacy
doc.privacy.lede: What we collect, what we do not, and why.
doc.privacy.body:
## What we do not collect
No account, no name, no email. We use no tracking cookies, no analytics profiles and no advertising.

## Your personal data
A CPF, a CNPJ, your NIS, health data and card details are personal data in Brazil (Lei 13.709/2018). We never ask for them. If you paste one into the conversation, the system removes it before sending and tells you so.

## Your questions
Your question is sent to our server to write the answer and is not stored. Conversations are not kept on our servers and are never used to profile anyone.

## What stays on your device
Recent conversations, plans and checklists you save live in this browser's local storage, on this device only. “Clear this device” removes them all.

## Abuse protection
We count requests per network address for a few minutes to hold off automated abuse. We keep only a scrambled form of the address, in memory, and it is never written to disk.
doc.accessibility.title: Accessibility
doc.accessibility.lede: The standard this service aims at, and what it already delivers.
doc.accessibility.body:
## Our standard
Ask Brasil aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1, level AA.

## What we do
- Everything works from the keyboard, with a visible focus indicator.
- Answers are announced by screen readers when ready, and every tool has a text alternative.
- Contrast meets AA in light and dark, and motion is reduced when your device asks for it.
- Portuguese and English have a full, reviewed interface.

## Known limits
- Interfaces in other languages have not yet been reviewed by native speakers.
- Maps come with a text list alongside them.
doc.terms.title: Terms
doc.terms.lede: What this service is, and what it does not do.
doc.terms.body:
## Information, not advice
Ask Brasil gives general information based on official sources. It is not legal, financial or medical advice, and it can be wrong. Always confirm on the official page before you apply, pay or decide.

## Independent service
Ask Brasil is not the Federal Government. Programme names and the information belong to the ministries.

## Fair use
Do not use the service to harm others, to commit fraud, or to overload it with automated requests. We may limit requests so it stays available to everyone.

## Emergencies
Ask Brasil is not an emergency channel. In an emergency call 192 (SAMU), 190 (Military Police) or 193 (Fire). In a mental health crisis call 188 (CVV).
